output_units.source_text:
<STRUCT_0001>
Papers discussing Hilbert schemes and the like.
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> Vistoli: <EMPHOPEN_0001>The Hilbert stack and the theory of moduli of families<EMPHCLOSE_0001>
<REF_0001>
<STRUCT_0004>
If <MATH_0001> is a algebraic stack separated and locally of finite type
over a locally Noetherian and locally separated algebraic space <MATH_0002>, Vistoli
defines the Hilbert stack <MATH_0003>
parameterizing finite and unramified morphisms from proper schemes.
It is claimed without proof that <MATH_0004>
is an algebraic stack. As a consequence, it is proved that with <MATH_0005>
as above, the Hom stack <MATH_0006> is an
algebraic stack if <MATH_0007> is proper and flat over <MATH_0008>.
<STRUCT_0005>
<STRUCT_0006> Olsson, Starr: <EMPHOPEN_0002>Quot functors for Deligne-Mumford stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0002>
<REF_0002>
<STRUCT_0007>
If <MATH_0009> is a Deligne-Mumford stack separated and locally of finite
presentation over an algebraic space <MATH_0010> and <MATH_0011> is a locally
finitely-presented <MATH_0012>-module, the quot functor
<MATH_0013> is represented by an algebraic
space separated and locally of finite presentation over <MATH_0014>. This paper
also defines generating sheaves and proves existence of a generating sheaf
for tame, separated Deligne-Mumford stacks which are global quotient stacks
of a scheme by a finite group.
<STRUCT_0008>
<STRUCT_0009> Olsson: <EMPHOPEN_0003>Hom-stacks and Restrictions of Scalars<EMPHCLOSE_0003>
<REF_0003>
<STRUCT_0010>
Suppose <MATH_0015> and <MATH_0016> are Artin stacks locally of finite
presentation over an algebraic space <MATH_0017> with finite diagonal with
<MATH_0018> proper and flat over <MATH_0019> such that fppf-locally on <MATH_0020>,
<MATH_0021> admits a finite finitely presented flat cover by an algebraic
space (eg. <MATH_0022> is Deligne-Mumford or a tame Artin stack).
Then <MATH_0023> is an Artin stack locally
of finite presentation over <MATH_0024>.
<STRUCT_0011>
<STRUCT_0012> Alexeev and Knutson: <EMPHOPEN_0004>Complete moduli spaces of branchvarieties<EMPHCLOSE_0004>
(<REF_0004>)
<STRUCT_0013>
They define a branchvariety of <MATH_0025> as a finite morphism
<MATH_0026> from a <EMPHOPEN_0005>reduced<EMPHCLOSE_0005> scheme <MATH_0027>. They prove
that the moduli stack of branchvarieties with fixed Hilbert polynomial and
total degrees of <MATH_0028>-dimensional components is a proper Artin stack with
finite stabilizer. They compare the stack of branchvarieties with the
Hilbert scheme, Chow scheme and moduli space of stable maps.
<STRUCT_0014>
<STRUCT_0015> Lieblich: <EMPHOPEN_0006>Remarks on the stack of coherent algebras<EMPHCLOSE_0006>
<REF_0005>
<STRUCT_0016>
This paper constructs a generalization of Alexeev and Knutson's stack of
branch-varieties over a scheme <MATH_0029> by building the stack as a stack of
algebras over the structure sheaf of <MATH_0030>. Existence proofs of <MATH_0031>
and <MATH_0032> spaces are given.
<STRUCT_0017>
<STRUCT_0018> Starr: <EMPHOPEN_0007>Artin's axioms, composition, and moduli spaces<EMPHCLOSE_0007>
<REF_0006>
<STRUCT_0019>
As an application of the main result, a common generalization of Vistoli's
Hilbert stack <REF_0007> and Alexeev and Knutson's stack of
branchvarieties <REF_0008> is provided. If <MATH_0033> is
an algebraic stack locally of finite type over an excellent scheme <MATH_0034>
with finite diagonal, then the stack <MATH_0035> parameterizing morphisms
<MATH_0036> from a proper algebraic space <MATH_0037> with a
<MATH_0038>-ample line bundle <MATH_0039> is an Artin stack locally of finite type over <MATH_0040>.
<STRUCT_0020>
<STRUCT_0021> Lundkvist and Skjelnes:
<EMPHOPEN_0008>Non-effective deformations of Grothendieck's Hilbert functor<EMPHCLOSE_0008>
<REF_0009>
<STRUCT_0022>
Shows that the Hilbert functor of a non-separated scheme is not represented
since there are non-effective deformations.
<STRUCT_0023>
<STRUCT_0024> Halpern-Leistner and Preygel:
<EMPHOPEN_0009>Mapping stacks and categorical notions of properness<EMPHCLOSE_0009>
<REF_0010>
<STRUCT_0025>
This paper gives a proof that the Hom stack is algebraic under some
hypotheses on source and target which are more general than, or at
least different from, the ones in Olsson's paper.
<STRUCT_0026>
<STRUCT_0027>
